name: Tomás — competent, current, and his wing has never been the problem
summary: Around 150 hours, 60 or so thermic, flying two or three times a month on proper thermic days, centres a climb, works the brakes. His mid-B has never actually stopped him doing anything. Most of his group have moved to high-Bs and he doesn't want to be the one left behind. He'd rather just fly the new wing than spend weeks easing into it, and he hasn't looked into what would change.
why_this_persona: The step's signature red flag, and the case the 'aspirational_rather_than_demonstrated' gate was written for. Four sources — Seb Ospina, Advance, Gin and Hamerton on Cloudbase Mayhem — converge on this being the thing to watch at this boundary, in different words. He is deliberately NOT weak: his thermic hours clear the figure, his currency is fine, his handling is adequate. The only thing wrong is that nothing in his flying has asked for the wing yet.

notes: Computed skills 70.8, psychological 52.7, total 62.7, no bonus.

EXACTLY ONE GATE, and it is the step-specific one. 'aspirational_rather_than_demonstrated' fires because wing_limiting_evidence is 'not really' AND his motive is on the gate's list. Note the gate would also have fired on the skills-below-65 branch or the thermic-hours branch; neither applies to him, which is the point — the motive branch is what catches an otherwise competent pilot.

IMPORTANT NEGATIVE: 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' must NOT fire. He matches its first clause (keep_up_with_group) but none of its second clause: skills 70.8 is above 65, his hands are active, he didn't freeze in a collapse and he keeps flying when it's rough. That negative case is the more important one to lock down, per knowledge/disagreements.md point 9 — a comparison-driven motive must not cap a pilot whose readiness evidence is genuinely there. A scorer that fires both gates has made the second clause too loose.
'ambition_without_readiness' must NOT fire either: he ticks longer_xc, but his skills score is 70.8, well above the gate's 55 threshold. Ambition alone never costs a band.

'time_on_current_wing' must not fire — his current_wing_time is 50_100, above that suggestion's trigger bands. The wing-hasn't-limited-you point reaches him through the direct question instead, which is the division of labour between those two suggestions.

TONE CHECK: this is the hardest message in the rubric to get right. The gate message has to tell a competent, current pilot that his own answer about his own wing is the thing stopping him, without reading as an accusation about his motives. It does that by naming the four sources, saying plainly that it isn't a criticism, and ending on the performance still sitting in his current wing. Required by docs/design-context.md's tone rule.

Of the three Not yet personas with decent skills (04, 05, 09), each is capped by a different mechanism — a currency gate, a demonstrated-readiness gate, and a category floor. None is capped by the total.
